correctness.rationale: The joint bivariate excursion height/duration generating function follows from a two-point gambler-ruin boundary recurrence, with D_h(z)=z(F_h(z)-F_(h-1)(z)). Explicit geometric maximum-height tails imply Hmax=(log n)/alpha+O_P(1). The analytic quasi-power conditional transform gives centered duration variance 8pq/delta^3 per height; mixing at the depth-selected maximum yields variance 8pq/(delta^3 alpha) per log n. The independent Catalan first-return formula gives both strict and weak length tails Theta(t^(-3/2) exp(-beta*t)). Chernoff-uniform empirical tail counts over O(log n) deterministic even thresholds may then be safely evaluated at the depth-selected random duration, yielding the rank expansion and joint normal law. All constants, parity/ties and parameter endpoints are explicitly handled. A standalone checker passed 424 finite algebraic diagnostics; these are not presented as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: A concrete second-order probability law for the deepest episode's empirical duration rank is not stated or shown to follow directly from either closely relevant inspected primary text. Wu (2026) establishes a first-order rank power, while Perfilev–Wachtel (2019) provide conditional single-excursion length normal limits. The new adaptive-threshold empirical-rank identity, lattice Catalan prefactor, explicit variance and joint normal limit require additional nontrivial steps. Actual research-record and literature searches returned no equivalent or stronger covering result. This is a provisional bounded-literature priority assessment, not proof of global uniqueness.
